messages:
maria: quick check — integrating new Python SDK into our backend. Need to: 1) customize User-Agent to include MyApp/1.2.3, 2) fully opt out of client metrics/telemetry (privacy req), and 3) ensure tracing propagation (traceparent) still works. also seeing retries causing duplicate events on streaming. any recommended config or pitfalls?

ashwin: short answers: set UA via client headers, use the metrics opt-out flag, and let the SDK propagate standard trace headers (traceparent). for streaming retries: treat streams as non-idempotent — prefer reconnect logic on failures rather than automatic retry. example (py):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(
    api_key="sk_live_...",
    default_headers={"User-Agent": "MyApp/1.2.3"},
    metrics_enabled=False,  # disables client telemetry/usage pings
    propagate_tracing=True, # SDK will forward traceparent/baggage if present
)
# when streaming, do manual reconnects to avoid duplicate side effects
```

kevin: for Go: the SDK exposes options, and you should also ensure your http.Client preserves context-based tracing. example: 
```go
client := redwood.NewClient("SK_...", redwood.WithUserAgent("MyApp/1.2.3"), redwood.WithTelemetryDisabled())
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body) // keep ctx with traceparent
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```
Note: net/http will carry W3C trace headers if your tracer injects them into ctx.

sarah: small gotcha — we had a bug where metrics_enabled=False still left a tiny keepalive ping on streaming connections (internal header: x-rd-heartbeat). if you need zero egress for compliance, beware. file created: GH #4217.

devex-bot: issue created -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4217 (streaming heartbeat when telemetry disabled)

ashwin: thanks @sarah — fix is merged to main and will be in next patch release. in the meantime, you can set the env var REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS=false and also set REDWOOD_STREAM_HEARTBEAT=0 to force no heartbeats. example env: `REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS=false REDWOOD_STREAM_HEARTBEAT=0`

maria: perfect. one last question — if bearer tokens rotate mid-stream, should we expect the stream to terminate? do we have a recommended pattern?

kevin: yes — token checks are performed on connection and periodically for long-lived sockets. typical pattern: short-lived streams + reauth via reconnect. if you need seamless rotation, implement a small-sidecar that re-establishes streams with new token and resumes state server-side, or keep operations idempotent.

maria: great, thanks everyone :thumbsup: will add notes to our integration guide and ping once deployed.
